$comment: Typeface pairings for the design system. All are free Google Fonts under the SIL Open Font License, so they work on the web, in print and in Figma/Adobe after installing. A brand picks one in products/<brand>/brand.json -> typography.pairing. fit: how well the pairing suits the Humanist Minimal approach (core = recommended, good = works, accent = for special cases).

pairings.name: Warm Modern
pairings.mood: Friendly and current. The headline face has slightly irregular, ink-trap details that echo hand-drawn line; the body face is open and calm.

pairings.name: Modern Editorial
pairings.mood: Quiet and elegant. A condensed, high-contrast serif for big headlines over a crisp, neutral sans.
pairings.bestFor: Culture, design, publishing, premium services. Big poster headlines.

display.case: Sentence case; italic for one emphasised word

pairings.name: Humanist Classic
pairings.mood: Calm, trustworthy, extremely readable. A true humanist superfamily: serif, sans and mono designed together.
pairings.bestFor: Education, health, non-profits, long reading, anything with lots of text.

pairings.name: Friendly
pairings.mood: Soft and approachable without being childish. A warm, chunky serif headline with a round, modern sans.

pairings.name: Calligraphic Humanist
pairings.mood: The most 'hand-made' of the set: letterforms built from a broad-nib pen. Literary and warm.

body.style: Humanist sans from the same family

pairings.name: Single-Family Minimal
pairings.mood: One family, strict and modern; hierarchy comes from size and weight only. The most minimal option.
pairings.bestFor: Tech, products, studios that want maximum restraint.

pairings.name: Soft Serif
pairings.mood: Bouncy, soft-cornered serif with a gentle humanist sans. Charming; use with restraint (one weight, no 'wonky' extras).

pairings.name: Technical Humanist
pairings.mood: Engineered but warm: a grotesque with humanist touches, with matching serif and mono. Precise without feeling cold.

scale.$comment: Type sizes are steps of a ratio from the base size. Names match roles used by the templates.

rules: Two families at most (display + body), plus a mono for small data such as dates, prices and codes.
Sentence case everywhere. All capitals only for short labels of one to three words, with letter-spacing.
Three sizes per piece is usually enough: headline, body, small.
Big headlines get tight leading (about 1.0) and slightly negative tracking; body text gets 1.5 leading and lines of 45-75 characters.
Left-align text. Centre only one or two short lines on a centred poster.
No handwriting or marker fonts: the human hand lives in the illustration, not the type.
